Apify web-search and web-fetch 2026-11-11 of official sources listed in each fact

facts.claim: Astir of Paros describes itself as a five-star hotel 'only a breath away from the quaint village of Naoussa'; its structured address is Kolymbithres, Naoussa, Paros 84 401. Accommodation pages listed: Executive Suites, Junior Sea View Suites, Premium Suites, Junior Suites and Interconnecting Junior Suites. Total room count not stated on the home page read.

Astir of Paros has its own Weddings page ('Dream Wedding in Paros'), saying the complex faces the Aegean Sea and offers 'an once-in-a-lifetime experience for a cherished wedding ceremony and a memorable reception', with the executive chef and team, decoration and 'personalized services'. The page (last modified 5 November 2018) states no capacity, ceremony locations, ceremony types or exclusive use.
Astir of Paros site navigation also lists an Art Gallery, Conferences & Events, Dining & Bars and Experiences pages, alongside Weddings.

Astir of Paros' Conferences & Events page says its Venus Conference Hall has 'a sitting capacity of 130 delegates' (conference seating, not a stated wedding capacity). Page last modified 5 November 2018.
facts.conflicts: Only capacity figure on the site is for conference seating; no wedding reception or ceremony capacity is published.

facts.claim: FAILURE: parilio.com home page fetched live returned an empty 114-byte document (no title, no links); Parilio could not be verified as a wedding venue from its own site.
FAILURE: portoparos.gr and cosmehotel.com (guessed official domains for Porto Paros and Cosme) both timed out after 60 seconds on a live fetch; neither verified. Not retried.

Akti Resort (own site weddingparos.gr) describes itself as a 'traditional Cycladic complex' within walking distance of Kolymbithres beach, 2.5 km from the fishing village of Naoussa, in the northwest of Paros, with a panoramic view of the bay of Naoussa. Address given as Naoussa, GR-84401 Paros.

Akti Resort says its social event reception hall hosts weddings, christenings and birthdays; the hall is 'situated next to the pool', has a panoramic view of the bay of Naoussa and can 'accommodate up to 350 guests'. It offers a menu of traditional Parian dishes with wine of its own production, plus 'free organisational consulting, without any commission' for suppliers such as photographer, florist and decorations. The site describes receptions; it does not state ceremony locations or ceremony types.

Akti Resort offers seven fully equipped apartments (double, triple or four beds) 'just 10 meters away from the sea', a pool and pool bar, and the family-run Restaurant 'Spiros', founded by the Vionis family (first taverna in Naoussa in 1966; reception area opened 2008). Exclusive use not stated. The site also shows room rates and template placeholder text, so it appears not recently maintained; rates not recorded here.
facts.conflicts: Page carries a leftover 'Our Services' block (golf course, pizza delivery) that does not match the property, and two different emails (info@weddingparos.gr and info@akti-studios.gr); treat the page as dated. Also says 'More info at www.aktiresortparos.gr' (not read).

facts.claim: FAILURE: Lilly Residence (Naoussa) official site navigation, read live, lists Stay, Facilities, Experiences, Location and suites but no weddings or events page; not verified as a wedding venue.

OUT OF AREA (lead for batch B): Paros Agnanti Resort & Spa's own site gives its address as Krios Beach, Parikia 84400 (five-star) and its navigation lists an Events page; it is on the Parikia side, not Naoussa and the north, so not assessed in batch A.

Astir of Paros says the hotel 'comprises 46 suites of 2-4 persons (4 executive and 42 junior ones) and 11 double rooms', surrounded by lush tropical gardens with views over the Kolymbithres bay; renovated completely in 2018, with Naxos white marble bathrooms and verandas or balconies over 'the golf course and the shimmering blue sea'. Interiors display works from the owners' private art collection.
FAILURE: a rendered (browser) fetch of parilio.com timed out after 60 seconds, following the empty plain fetch in fact_05. Parilio not verified; not retried again.

Monastiri Beach Bar & Restaurant's own Weddings page says it sits within Paros Park, 'steps away from the historic Monastiri of Saint Ioannis Detis', 'just a 10-minute drive from Naoussa', reachable by road or by sea thanks to its dock. Couples can exchange vows 'on the sandy beach' or host a reception in the restaurant; event spaces listed are the amphitheatre, restaurant, lounge and beach deck. A wedding brochure is offered for download (not read).

Monastiri says its 'Archilochos' amphitheatre, built into the natural stone of the slope, 'can seat up to 800 guests comfortably' (stated in the corporate section). It also hosts pre and post-wedding parties with a stage and beach. Monastiri is a beach bar and restaurant: no accommodation is offered on the page read; wedding capacity for the restaurant or beach and exclusive use are not stated.
facts.conflicts: 800 is the amphitheatre seating figure given for corporate events, not a wedding capacity.

facts.claim: Anemoi Paros Hotel Resort (anemoiresort.gr, redirects to parosresort.com) says it is 'within a small distance from the village of Naoussa', overlooking Naoussa bay, and 'comprises eight apartments and studios, hosting from 2 to 6 people' in traditional Cycladic style, with an outdoor pool and Jacuzzi. Its Weddings section says the small Chapel of St. John, built in traditional Cycladic architecture, is on the premises and suits a wedding ceremony or a baptism. Capacity and exclusive use not stated on the home page read.
facts.conflicts: Home page says 'eight apartments and studios' but lists eight room types (one Executive Suite for up to 8 persons), so the count may be of types, not units; check before stating a room count.

facts.claim: OUT OF AREA (lead for batch C): Calme Boutique Hotel's own site (calme.gr redirects to calmehotelparos.com) gives its address as Chryssi Akti, Drios, describes itself as adults only, and search-result navigation shows 'Symbolic Weddings', 'Renewal of Vows' and 'Wedding Proposals' pages (not read). Not assessed in batch A.

Akti Paros's current site (aktiresortparos.gr, Venue Hall page) says it hosts 'weddings and baptisms', has a private pool overlooking the bay of Naoussa with the sea 'just a few meters from the pool area', and a space with unobstructed views of the bay 'able to accommodate up to 350 guests', with a traditional Parian menu; guests can book rooms at the property. Confirms the 350 figure in fact_08.

Anemoi's Weddings & Events page says the ceremony can take place in the small Chapel of St. John on the premises, after which staff organise a reception 'in our beautiful area by the swimming pool, with the deep blue of the Aegean Sea in the background'. No guest capacity or exclusive use is stated. The wording does not name a ceremony type, so whether religious ceremonies can be held in the chapel is not confirmed.

Pyrgaki Hotel describes itself as a '4* Boutique Hotel in Paros' and says it is 'situated in a truly enchanting location with stunning views to the gulf of Parikia'; it offers weddings ('There is no better way to celebrate the most romantic day of your life, than a romantic wedding in Paros').

Pyrgaki Hotel wedding page, ceremony options as stated: 'Whether you choose to get married in St. George chapel in Pyrgaki hotel or in One Hundred Doors historical and popular byzantine church in Parikia, your wedding reception by the privileged pool will exceed your expectations.'

Pyrgaki Hotel lists services it can offer: 'Fireworks, live orchestra, dj, superb cuisine, a romantic horse-drawn carriage for the bride and a luxurious white car for the groom, a beautiful honeymoon suite'. The wedding page publishes no guest capacity, room count or exclusive-use terms (page last modified 2020-09-11 per its metadata).

The Secret View describes itself as 'an event venue, located on the island of Paros in Greece, on the hills above Golden Beach' on a '40-acre estate' hosting weddings. Its map link points to Tzanes (844 00). This places it on the east coast, outside Batch B's area (Parikia, west and inland); passed to Batch C.

The Secret View, as stated: a 'traditional greek chapel as the backdrop of your ceremony or your couple's shoot', a 'spacious lower level terrace' for the reception, an 'upper level pergola' for cocktail hour and a 'stone outdoor salon with beige waterproof canopy'; 'romantic symbolic ceremony'; guests stay 'in the hotels nearby' (no rooms on site stated).
The Secret View FAQ: 'we ask our couples to stop the loud music at 2am' and couples have 'full access to our venue for 24h'. No guest capacity on the homepage read.

Roses Beach (site header 'Roses Paros Hotel') says it 'is the perfect venue for weddings in Paros, Greece'; 'The large reception area around the floodlit pool has spellbinding views across the tranquil bay of Parikia', with bougainvillea and palm trees.

Roses Beach, ceremony options as stated: 'Wedding ceremonies can be arranged to take place in the idyllic church of Agios Fokas, a short distance from the hotel, only metres away from the sea'; alternatively the hotel 'can help you find another church or wedding location'. It also says 'Civil weddings on Paros, either in the municipal offices or even on the beach have increased in popularity in recent years and we can help in all your arrangements.'

Roses Beach wedding page publishes no guest capacity, room count or exclusive-use terms; the reception is poolside in the hotel grounds. The page names a preferred photographer (a vendor name, not for use in copy).

Lefkes Village hotel (inland, Lefkes): live read of the presumed official site https://www.lefkesvillage.gr/ timed out after 60 seconds on 2026-11-11; no official page confirming weddings was read, so it is excluded (search results found only booking and review sites).

Roses Beach homepage: 'a small family run hotel with 14 double rooms, most with either sea or pool views', 'located just above Livadia Beach, a short walk from Paros Island's main town'; upper-floor rooms have 'unparalleled views over the entire bay and town of Parikia'. The poolside bar area is 'available for private hire' and 'a perfect setting for weddings'. The page describes itself as a 'cheap hotel with swimming pool', a positioning mismatch for a luxury-audience guide.

Yria Island Boutique Hotel & Spa (Parasporos, west coast): no official site page stating it hosts weddings was read; search returned only booking and reseller listings, and a live read of the presumed official domain https://www.yriaparos.gr/ timed out after 60 seconds on 2026-11-11. Excluded.

Villa Aethra (Butterfly Valley, inland west of Parikia, per third-party listings): no official website found in searches; only rental, booking and planner pages. Excluded under the live-official-read rule.

It also describes itself as a family-friendly hotel.

Golden Bay Paros (official site, V.I.P. Services page, read live) says Deluxe Villa One and Deluxe Villa Two are designed to connect into one large residence that can host an important event such as weddings or christenings, and that for this all Golden Bay rooms must be rented, including Suite 1 and Suite 2 on the first floor. Its booking form lists four units (Superior Suite One and Two, Deluxe Villa One and Two). The page does not state the property's area, guest capacity or ceremony options.
facts.conflicts: Area not stated on the page read; the name suggests Golden Beach but this is not confirmed.

facts.claim: Akti Resort (weddingparos.gr, official site, read live) offers a reception hall for weddings and seven rooms, but places itself within walking distance of Kolymbithres beach and 2.5 km from Naoussa, so it is in the north (batch A area), not the east or south coast. Poseidon of Paros: a guessed URL (https://www.poseidon-paros.gr/weddings) returned an image (HTTP 415), not a page; the hotel's own sitemap (read live) lists its weddings page at /weddings-reception-organizing, which was then read live (fact_207). facts.claim: Palmtree Events Paros (official site, read live, modified 25 September 2026) describes itself as a villa event venue in Paros for weddings, baptisms and parties, with a 400 square metre villa with sea views, couple accommodation for up to three days, catering, decoration, music and lighting packages, and an 'underwater wedding' option on its booking form. The page does not state which part of Paros it is in or a guest capacity, so it cannot be placed in the east and south coast group from this read.

Poseidon of Paros weddings page (official, read live, modified 26 June 2024, page title 'Paros Wedding Venues, Golden Beach') says the hotel sits next to Golden Beach, describes itself as a wedding venue with a chapel, ideal for beachside weddings, says it can cater to all wedding reception needs, and offers receptions by the pool or on Golden Beach, overlooking the Aegean. No guest capacity, ceremony types beyond the chapel, or exclusive-use terms are published on the page.

Golden Beach Hotel Paros weddings page (official, read live, modified 9 April 2021) says it is ideal for beachside weddings and special events with a spectacular Aegean view, cites 40 years of experience organising weddings and events, says it plans weddings, baptisms, follow-up receptions and private parties, and that 'the estate could support up to 350 people', with a buffet menu, classic seated style or free-style cocktail function. No ceremony location (chapel or beach) or exclusive-use terms are published.
facts.conflicts: The 350 figure is phrased as 'could support up to 350 people' without saying seated or standing; treat as a maximum, not a seated capacity.

facts.claim: The Rooster Antiparos (official 'Events' page, read live) describes itself as a lifestyle and wellness resort and says events there run 'from intimate ceremonies and shared dinners to larger celebrations', in spaces including the Secret Garden, The Bar at sunset, the Farm and the Beach House, handled by an events team. The page does not use the word 'wedding', and publishes no capacity, room count or exclusive-use terms, so it does not meet the inclusion rule (official site saying it hosts weddings).

The Municipality of Paros tourism site (imagine.paros.gr, which identifies itself as the Municipality of Paros (Dimos Parou) tourist site) has a Wedding and Honeymoon page saying ceremonies can be held at a country chapel or at Panagia Ekatontapiliani, with guests arriving at the church by boat, yacht, speed boat, horse-drawn carriage or on foot with musicians. It names favourite churches including Panagia Ekatontapiliani, Agia Anna in Pandroso, Agios Fokas at the entrance to the port of Parikia, Agios Ioannis in Kolybithres, Zoodochou Pigis in Lageri, Agios Nikolaos in Piso Livadi and Agios Nikolaos in Pyrgaki. The page gives no civil marriage steps, documents, lead times or fees.

The Municipality of Paros official site (paros.gr) staff directory lists, under its Department of Citizen Service, Civil and Municipal Status and Registry Office, a Civil Marriages section (Tomeas Politikon Gamon) and a Registry Office unit, both in the municipality's offices (phone prefix 22843601xx). No paros.gr page read on 11 November 2026 sets out civil marriage steps, documents, ceremony location, lead times or fees for foreigners, so the copy should say to check these with the Municipality of Paros and the Embassy, including any fees.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from mykonos-wedding-venues fact_309) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates; local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept ones issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from mykonos-wedding-venues fact_310) an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred here; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not work as proof of a name change, and it suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from mykonos-wedding-venues fact_311) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation by authentication or apostille. All notarial services need an appointment (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; apostilled documents and CNIs are ready for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged; the Embassy gives no legal advice, does not witness signatures on overseas documents, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and fees apply (amounts not recorded). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data by City' page has no Paros station; for the South Aegean it lists Naxos and Rodos. The Naxos station (lat 37.081, lon 25.369, altitude 3 m; data period not stated on the page) shows mean monthly maximum temperatures of 22.1 C in May, 25.9 C in June, 27.1 C in July, 27.0 C in August, 25.1 C in September and 21.9 C in October.

HNMS Naxos station (nearest official station to Paros, labelled as Naxos) shows mean precipitation days of 3.6 in May, 1.1 in June, 0.4 in July, 0.3 in August, 1.9 in September and 5.5 in October (6.0 in April), and a prevailing wind direction of north in every month, with monthly mean wind power highest in winter and 13.3 to 13.9 in July to September (units as shown on the page, not labelled).

Visit Greece (the official Greek tourism site) says Paros lies at the centre of the Cyclades and lists flights from Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) to Paros Airport of about 45 minutes and from Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia) of about 1 hour 15 minutes. It also notes Parian marble was used for works including Praxiteles' Hermes and the Venus de Milo.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice (updated 30 September 2026, still current at 11 November 2026) is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (level green). It says heatwaves are frequent over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion, heat stroke and death, and wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September, including near tourist locations on the mainland and the islands, prompting evacuations; local alerts come from 112 to mobile phones.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says lifeguards operate at many Greek beaches from June to September, sea conditions can change quickly with strong currents and rips, and its latest update advises care when swimming (boat traffic, coastal hazards, currents, marine life) and swimming at patrolled beaches where possible.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says ferries and large catamarans carry most visitors to the Greek islands; in the May to October tourist season expect high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports; you will usually carry luggage up and down stairs; ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds, so reconfirm departures; and arrange a coach or taxi in advance. It also says Australians can visit the Schengen area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period and must register biometrics under the EES on arrival.

The Municipality of Paros tourism site (imagine.paros.gr) says flights to Paros depart from Eleftherios Venizelos Airport in Athens and take approximately 45 minutes, and that Paros Airport (code PAS) is 9 kilometres southwest of Parikia, at Voutakos, Agkairia. It lists Olympic Air and Sky Express contacts. No official airport-operator website for Paros Airport was found within the time limit.

The Municipality of Paros tourism site says the island's main port is at Parikia, reachable by sea 365 days a year from Piraeus and Rafina; only strong westerly winds create issues for the port. Naoussa has a harbour and an organised marina (vessels up to 3 m draft), with summer day cruises to Tinos, Mykonos and Delos and excursions to Naxos; Piso Livadi marina in the south is protected from the strong north winds and is the starting point for excursions to Amorgos, Koufonisia and Santorini; Pounta connects Paros and Antiparos all year, with ferries every 30 minutes and a crossing of about 10 minutes (last summer ferry from Antiparos to Pounta at 2.00am).

The Municipality of Paros tourism site says KTEL public buses link all villages with each other and with Parikia and Naoussa all year round, with summer routes (especially to Naoussa) running into the early morning; the Parikia KTEL station is next to the port. Main routes include Parikia to Naoussa, Parikia to Aliki, and loops via Lefkes, Marpissa, Piso Livadi, Logaras, Pounta, Chryssi Akti (Golden Beach) and Drios.

Petra Farm (petrafarm.gr) has a Weddings & Events page inviting couples to 'experience your magic day on our organic farm'. Petra Estate, built in the 1980s, is set high above the bay of Kolymbithres with views across to Naousa, among olive groves and a productive vineyard; address given as Kolimbithres, Paros 84401 (Naoussa and the north).

Petra Farm ceremony and celebration spaces as stated: a bridal suite in the rustic farmhouse for getting ready; ceremonies in the chapel's courtyard among olive trees, with the chapel (interior painted by two acclaimed Greek iconographers) accommodating 120 guests; a poolside cocktail area; dinner by the pool seating 80 guests; and an event space that 'comfortably fits 150 people and a dance floor'.

Petra Farm states it limits weddings to 10 per year, offers one point of contact for wedding enquiries, and is on site to oversee all vendor activities during the entire rental period, working with the couple's wedding planners. Guest accommodation room count is not published on the weddings page.

Astir of Paros (astirofparos.gr) describes itself as a 5 star hotel near the village of Naoussa; its schema address is Kolymbithres, Naoussa, Paros. It has a dedicated weddings page ('Dream Wedding in Paros') offering the setting 'for a cherished wedding ceremony and a memorable reception', with the executive chef's cuisine and personalised services.

Astir of Paros homepage: the St. Nicholas chapel, at the edge of the golf course right by the water, is 'an ideal choice for your wedding'; the grounds also hold the 12th-century Byzantine chapel of Panagia Angelochairetisti, carved in white Parian marble. The resort has tropical gardens with hundreds of palms, a small private sandy beach for guests next to Kolymbithres bay, two gourmet restaurants and two bars, and was fully renovated in 2018. No wedding capacity or room count is published on the pages read.

The Secret View at Fladakia Estate (the-secret-view.com, logo 'Fladakia Estate') is an event venue on Paros 'on the hills above Golden Beach' with a view of the Aegean, a 40-acre family estate hosting weddings, baptisms, corporate and private events (east and south coast).

The Secret View wedding spaces as stated: a traditional Greek chapel as the backdrop for the ceremony or couple's shoot, a spacious lower terrace for the reception, an upper-level pergola for cocktail hour, and a stone outdoor salon with a beige waterproof canopy for more intimate settings. It promotes a 'romantic symbolic ceremony with a view'.

The Secret View FAQ: guests stay in nearby hotels and the venue is 'happy to organize shuttles' (no on-site guest rooms stated); loud music stops at 2am out of respect for local villages, with an after-party (for example an acoustic band) possible; couples may bring their own vendors, with a catering site inspection suggested; prices include full access to the venue for 24 hours to use all areas. No guest capacity is published on the homepage.

The Secret View 'The Estate' page gives per-space layouts: Pergola (bamboo roof, covered, for drizzle or heat) ceremony 30 / dinner 35; Outdoor Salon (stone, beige canopy) ceremony 60 / dinner 70; Chapel (Greek chapel as ceremony backdrop, chairs facing church or view) ceremony 85 / dinner 90; Terrace (stone deck, 180 degree view, Aegean behind) ceremony 110 / dinner 120.

The same Secret View page also says the Terrace 'can fit up to 250 guests in a seated layout, with a dancefloor, a stage for your favourite live-band and a lounge area by the bar', which conflicts with the 120 dinner layout stated for the same space.

Mira Luxury Villas / Villa Mira Paros (villamiraparos.com) homepage: 'Say I Do Amidst Breathtaking Views... a premier wedding venue in Paros' with 'the exclusive option to book the entire property for your special day'; the property is 'perfect for gatherings, weddings, and parties' as you can rent the entire property with shared BBQ and pool area.

Villa Mira Paros has a central swimming pool with Aegean views and 4 villas with kitchens and dining areas, on a 7,500 square metre lot with panoramic views of the Aegean and the Bay of Paroikia, described as perched atop a mountain; contact page address given as Parikoia, Paros (Parikia and the west). No wedding guest capacity is published on the page read.

insider_details.detail: Kolymbithres has two very different scales side by side: Astir of Paros with 57 rooms (46 suites and 11 doubles) for a guest block under one roof, and Akti Paros with a 350-guest reception hall but only seven apartments, so a large Akti wedding needs guest rooms elsewhere around Naoussa.

Monastiri sits about a 10-minute drive from Naoussa beside the Monastiri of Saint Ioannis Detis and has its own dock, so guests staying in Naoussa can arrive by road or by boat; it has no rooms, so plan return transport at the end of the night.

Anemoi is the only batch A venue with its own chapel on site (Chapel of St. John) and a poolside reception area facing the Aegean, which keeps ceremony and reception in one place; with eight apartments it suits a small wedding party with most guests staying in Naoussa.

Capacity figures published in the north are not wedding figures: Astir's 130 is conference seating and Monastiri's 800 is amphitheatre seating for corporate events. Only Akti publishes a reception figure (350). Ask every venue for seated dinner and ceremony numbers separately.

Two of the west-side options frame the same view from different heights: Pyrgaki looks over the gulf of Parikia and Roses Beach sits just above Livadia Beach with views across the bay, so a sunset reception on this side of the island faces west over the water.

Roses Beach has only 14 double rooms, so a wedding there means booking most guests into other Parikia hotels; it suits couples who want a short walk from the main town rather than a self-contained resort stay.

Both Parikia hotels separate ceremony and reception: vows in a nearby church (Agios Fokas, St. George chapel or the Hundred Doors church in Parikia) and the reception back at the hotel pool, so plan the short transfer between the two and the timing around sunset.

Golden Beach is where both qualifying east-coast hotels sit, and they suit different briefs: Poseidon of Paros has its own chapel and pool or beach receptions, while Golden Beach Hotel publishes the only number in this group (up to 350 people), so a larger guest list starts there; get the seated figure in writing.

Golden Beach is a windsurfing beach (Golden Beach Hotel runs its own windsurfing station), so plan a beach reception with a sheltered pool-terrace or indoor fallback and ask each hotel for its wind plan.
Golden Bay Paros only offers weddings if every unit is rented, so treat it as an exclusive-use villa buyout for a small wedding party, not a guest-hotel block.
For an Antiparos note, Soros Beach is the one property whose own events page names a beach wedding ceremony; confirm this in writing before it is listed.

Civil weddings on Paros run through the Municipality's Civil Marriages section within its Registry Office, but no official checklist is published online, so start the CNI and apostille steps with the Australian Embassy in Athens early and confirm documents, lead times and fees with the Municipality in writing before setting a date.

Paros is a 45-minute flight from Athens, so a CNI or apostille appointment at the Embassy (weekdays, 9:00am to 12:30pm; documents ready within two working days) can be built into an Athens stopover before flying on.
Paros Airport sits about 9 km southwest of Parikia, and the main ferry port is in Parikia itself, so a guest welcome hub in or near Parikia keeps arrival transfers short whether guests fly or sail.

Ferries can be delayed or cancelled by strong winds and the nearest official station (Naxos) records a prevailing northerly wind in every month, so build a buffer day before the wedding for guests arriving by sea, and favour sheltered settings or a wind plan for outdoor ceremonies.

At the nearest HNMS station (Naxos), June to September averages under two rain days a month with mean highs of about 25 to 27 C, while Smartraveller warns of summer heatwaves and June to September wildfires; late-afternoon ceremonies with shade and water suit a July or August date, while May (about 22 C, 3.6 rain days) and September (about 25 C, 1.9 rain days) are milder.
Antiparos is about 10 minutes from Pounta by year-round car ferry every 30 minutes, which makes a pre-wedding or recovery day trip easy to schedule without private boats.

Petra Farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year and has a chapel courtyard for 120, poolside dinner for 80 and an event space for 150, so the guest count decides the reception space: under 80 stays by the pool, larger groups move a few steps to the event space.
The Secret View has no on-site guest rooms and offers shuttles from nearby hotels, so book a room block near Golden Beach and plan the return runs around its 2am loud-music stop.

At The Secret View, the bamboo-roofed pergola and the canopied stone salon are the covered spaces for heat or drizzle, but they seat only 35 and 70 for dinner, so a larger wedding has no fully covered dinner space published; agree a heat and wind plan for the terrace.
Villa Mira Paros can be booked whole, with four villas and a shared pool above the Bay of Paroikia, which suits a wedding party staying together close to the port town.
Astir of Paros and Petra Farm both sit at Kolymbithres on the bay facing Naoussa, so couples can pair a hotel stay with a nearby estate ceremony without a long island transfer.

open_questions.question: Batch A qualifies 4 in Naoussa and the north: Astir of Paros (five-star, Kolymbithres), Anemoi Paros Hotel Resort (Naoussa, on-site chapel), Monastiri Beach Bar & Restaurant (Agios Ioannis Detis, beach ceremonies, no rooms) and Akti Paros (Kolymbithres, 350-guest reception hall, seven apartments, family-run, not luxury). Include Akti or hold as reserve?
Out-of-area leads for other batches: Paros Agnanti Resort & Spa (Krios Beach, Parikia, has Events page) for batch B; Calme Boutique Hotel (Chryssi Akti, Drios, symbolic weddings pages) for batch C.

Batch B qualified 2 venues in its area: Pyrgaki Hotel (Parikia gulf) and Roses Beach (above Livadia Beach, Parikia). Roses Beach calls itself a 'cheap hotel' with 14 double rooms: include for a AUD 150k+ audience, or hold as a reserve? Neither publishes capacity.
The Secret View (fact_103 to fact_105) qualified on a live read but sits above Golden Beach (east coast): hand to Batch C to avoid duplication. Petra Farm (Kolymbithres) is a lead for Batch A.

No inland (Lefkes, Marpissa, Prodromos) or winery venue qualified within the time limit; a top-up batch could retry Lefkes Village via a different fetch route, as both official-domain fetches timed out (not declined).

Batch C qualifies 2 Paros venues, both at Golden Beach (Poseidon of Paros, Golden Beach Hotel Paros), plus Golden Bay Paros as a conditional reserve (location unconfirmed) and Soros Beach Antiparos for a short Antiparos note (with VERIFY). No qualifying venue found in Drios, Piso Livadi, Logaras or Aliki within the time limit. The Rooster Antiparos excluded (no wedding wording). Akti Resort is north (batch A); Palmtree Events Paros is unplaced.

RUN REPORT ONLY: no official Municipality of Paros page on civil marriage for foreigners could be found or read (searches of paros.gr returned only a staff directory listing a Civil Marriages section and Registry Office, and a 2015 council decision on Chinese couples' weddings, not read). No gov.gr civil marriage page was found in search (news articles only, not used). Copy should therefore say: check with the Municipality of Paros and the Embassy, including any fees. Paros Airport has no operator website found; airport and port facts come from imagine.paros.gr, the municipality's own tourism site.

Batch E qualifies 4 venues by live official-site reads: Petra Farm (Kolymbithres, Naoussa and the north; fact_400 to fact_402), Astir of Paros (Kolymbithres, Naoussa and the north; fact_403, fact_404), The Secret View at Fladakia Estate (hills above Golden Beach, east and south coast; fact_405 to fact_409) and Villa Mira Paros (above Parikia bay, Parikia and the west; fact_410, fact_411). Not qualified in time (no official site located in search, or not reached before the 12-minute limit): Blue Mare Villas, Villa Aethra (only VRBO and editorial results), Parilio (no official result), Anthemion Villas & Suites (no official result), Cove Paros (only Instagram and planner results), Costa Pounda (no official result), Monastiri, Orbis, Palmtree Events Paros (only TikTok and Instagram results; the palmtreeweddingevents.com site is a Brentwood, California venue, not Paros). Note Petra Farm and Astir sit at Kolymbithres, which batch A (Naoussa) may also cover: dedupe.
